title: Part-of-Speech Abbreviation

illustrates.quote: Ignore font attributes used with parts-of-speech abbreviations (with or without punctuation), e.g., v. or v for verb, n. or n for noun, m. or m for masculine, f. or f for feminine in dictionaries and glossaries. Note this change on the Transcriber’s Notes page.

blocks.features: Single dictionary-style glossary-entry line: headword 'accuse' bold, phonetic respelling '(uh-KUZ)' plain (possibly small caps — modest source resolution), part-of-speech abbreviation 'v.' italic, definition 'blame' plain.

print.notes: No heading; the box is a single glossary-entry line.
print.surroundingText: Follows rule 5.3.4 directly, on printed page 5-4.
print.printFeatures: Single boxed dictionary-entry line, black serif text.

braille.notes: One line, flush left, margin 8 stripped. No typeform indicators: both the bold headword and the italic 'v.' abbreviation are dropped, per 5.3.4; ';v4' is the ordinary UEB way of writing the abbreviation 'v.', not a font-attribute indicator.

uncertain: The exact print styling of the phonetic respelling '(uh-KUZ)' (plain vs. small caps) is read from a modest-resolution page image; it does not affect the braille, which drops it as ordinary un-emphasized text either way.
resolution: No disagreement on substance; both runs read the same single boxed line. Braille independently re-derived from .txt line 3925 (margin 8), byte-identical to both runs.
